subject: Silverline AI connector — commercial & data-residency carveouts
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@silverline.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@silverline.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft SOW + a couple of carveouts we need to highlight

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Attaching our draft SOW and MSA excerpt for the connector work (Silverline_SOW_v1.docx). Two quick things from our side that need to be visible up front:

- Data residency: Silverline will persist user-level logs for 90 days in our EU region for troubleshooting. We need a carveout so those logs are excluded from Redwoods DPA residency guarantee when the customer selects Redwood-hosted EU model variants.
- Indemnity & caps: Our legal ops requests indemnity limited to direct damages capped at 2x annual fees for connector-related incidents. No open-ended indemnity.

Can you loop in procurement/legal at Redwood for any high-level objections? Were OK to iterate quickly — hoping to get a signed SOW by end of month so we can start integration work.

Attachments: Silverline_SOW_v1.docx

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Partnerships | Silverline AI
A: aisha.khan@silverline.ai | M: +1 415-555-0192

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@silverline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + a couple of carveouts we need to highlight

Aisha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the SOW + MSA excerpt. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Kimberly (procurement) to review the carveouts you flagged. Ben will be our integration PM on the project.

High-level: were generally comfortable with an operational carveout for short-lived troubleshooting logs, but well need firm language around whats stored, retention, access controls, and how it interacts with our DPA commitments. On indemnity, that sounds like a constructive starting point — legal to propose language.

Marissa / Kimberly — please see attachments from Silverline and advise on the specific redlines we should request. If possible, Marissa, can you provide editable redline language we can send back to Aisha this week?

Next step: Ill propose a short sync on Thursday if that helps move things along (30 minutes).

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
L: logan_wright@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@silverline.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + a couple of carveouts we need to highlight

Logan / Aisha —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the SOW and MSA excerpt and drafted a short set of requested redlines (attached: Redwood_requested_redlines_v1.docx). Key asks (summary):

1) Data residency carveout: add explicit definition for "troubleshooting logs" (fields, retention 90 days, pseudonymization where feasible), and an explicit statement that these logs do not constitute customer data under section 2.1 of the DPA.

2) Subprocessors: require notice + 30-day review window for new subprocessors for connector-hosted processing; if Silverline uses cloud logging providers outside the EEA, require SOC2 report and contractual flow-downs.

3) Incident response & notification: 24-hour initial notification for incidents affecting confidentiality; 72-hour follow-up with root cause and mitigation.

4) Indemnity cap: we can accept a negotiated monetary cap tied to fees, but we prefer a higher multiplier (3x annual fees) for connector work where personal data is involved. If youre firm on 2x, wed like to carve out intentional misconduct.

5) Termination for convenience / cure: propose a 30-day cure for material breach; shorter windows make it hard for integration teams.

Please review the attached redline language and indicate which points we should prioritize versus escalate to commercial. If Silverline can provide SOC2 and a subprocessors list now, that will speed approvals.

Marissa Cole
Principal Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Contracts Team <contracts@silverline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@silverline.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + a couple of carveouts we need to highlight

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear redlines. A few clarifications from Silverline legal:

- SOC2 / subprocessors: SOC2 report (type II, 2026) is available here: https://drive.internal/soc2/silverline-report-2026.pdf. Attached is our current subprocessors list (silverline_subprocessors_list.csv). Were using LogStream Inc. for ephemeral logs (EU region), which is SOC2 certified.
- Indemnity: we prefer the 2x-fees cap and would resist a higher multiplier. Were open to carving out intentional misconduct, but want to avoid open-ended exceptions that could create insurance issues.
- Termination / cure: we can accept a 30-day cure for material breach but would like a 15-day cure for minor data-handling discrepancies so we dont lose integration work over transient issues.

Weve attached the subprocessors list and updated SOW for your review. Happy to talk through the remaining items; if acceptable, we can push a DocuSign envelope to get the SOW & MSA (DS link below).

Attachments: silverline_subprocessors_list.csv
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/teams/silverline/ds-12345

Regards,
Silverline Contracts Team
contracts@silverline.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Contracts Team <contracts@silverline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + a couple of carveouts we need to highlight

Aisha / Silverline team —

Thanks for the SOC2 link and the subprocessors list. A couple of procurement items to confirm before we circulate a final counterparty-ready package:

- Billing / fees: confirm whether connector work will be invoiced as a one-time integration fee (in the SOW) or as recurring setup + usage fees. We need line items for accounting and a PO.
- Acceptance criteria: please add an explicit acceptance checklist to the SOW (integration smoke tests, latency targets, and a rollback plan).
- DocuSign flow: once legal flags are resolved we can accept a DocuSign envelope, please mark the envelope as "SOW + MSA for connector".

If youre OK, well propose the following next steps: (1) Marissa and Silverline legal agree on redline language for data residency/indemnity this week; (2) Silverline confirms billing model; (3) we schedule a 30-min handoff call (calendar link below) and then push DocuSign.

Calendar: https://calendar.redwood.com/meetings/5e9a-connector-term-sync

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@silverline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + a couple of carveouts we need to highlight

Team —

Thanks for the fast iteration. Consensus path looks clear: Silverline provides the SOC2 and subprocessors (received), Marissa to finalize redline language accepting a 2x cap with an intentional-misconduct carveout compromise, Kimberly to confirm billing model and acceptance criteria, and then DocuSign.

Ben — can you own the integration checklist (smoke tests + rollback) and share the draft by Wednesday EOD so Silverline can review?

Aisha — if youre aligned Ill hold a 30-minute sync on Thursday at the calendar link and we can close redlines and request the DocuSign envelope (Deal ID: DL-9843).

Appreciate the partnership — hoping to get this into execution next week.

Logan Wright
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
